SUBARACHNOID HAEMORRHAGE 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
 
ED MANAGEMENT  
 
Resus, Fluids & Monitoring 
*ABC approach 
*A – patient with decreased LOC have increased risk of  
         aspiration à intubate 
*C – maintain intravascular volume with isotonic fluids 
        Monitor for hyponatraemia 
        Target BP à MAP > 80-90 but < 130 mmHg 
        If MAP > 130 mmHg à Start Labetalol (see protocol) 
        In patients who are hypertensive ensure adequate  
        analgesia, nimodipine ± IV antihypertensive agent 
*D – if patient has seizures start anticonvulsant therapy (no  
         role for prophylactic ACT); nurse head up (unless c/i) 
 
History and Examination 
 
Investigations (see box) and monitoring 
*HR, BP, Sats, ECG 
 
Specific Treatment & Identify & Treat Complications 
*Vasospasm – prevention is NB! Maintain euvolaemia,  
                          avoid hypotension, Nimodipine, early surgery 
*Re-bleeding – avoid HPT, avoid increased/decreased ICP,   
                            sedation if agitated 
*Hydrocephalus 
*Pain – analgesia (see Pain Management protocol) 
*Standard neuroprotective measures 
 
Disposition 
*Neurosurgery referral 
CLINICAL FEATURES  
 
*Sudden onset of headache 
*Unusual headache for patient 
*Sentenal headache (40%) 
*Transient or persistent LOC 
*Vomiting 
*Seizures/posturing 
*Meningism 
*Neurological signs à according to area involved 
*Fundoscopy – retinal haemorrhage, papilloedema 
*Risk factors (see box) 
RISK FACTORS 
 
*Female 
*Age > 50 years 
*Hypertension 
*Smoking 
*Oral contraceptives 
*Alcohol history 
*Connective tissue disease 
*Polycystic kidney disease 
*Family history 
*Coarctation of the Aorta 
*Previous aneurysm/SAH 
INVESTIGATIONS 
 
Bedside 
*ECG – tall peaked t-waves, STD,   
  prolonged QT, arrythmia 
*Echo – neurogenic CMO 
 
Laboratory 
*FBC, U&E, CRP, INR/PTT, trop 
*Lumbar puncture 
 
Radiological 
*CXR – neurogenic pulmonary oedema 
*CTB  
*Digital subtraction angio (DSA) =   
  Gold Standard 
OTTAWA CLINICAL DECISION RULE OUT 
CRITERIA 
“ANT LEaF” 
 
A – Age > 40 
N – Neck pain or stiffness 
T – Thunderclap headcahe 
L – Loss of consciousness (witnessed) 
E – Exertion (onset during) 
and 
F – Flexion (limited neck flexion on examination) 
 
Patients require investigation if  
one or more findings present 
 
Dr R Gihwala CMJAH Emergency Department June 2020
